thread.title: UPDATE: Investors have been 'mindlessly' following this hot-stock strategy all year

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: Investors have been 'mindlessly' following this hot-stock strategy all year
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
Critical information for the U.S. trading day
Hope that Netflix might provide some added buoyancy to the broader equity market on Wednesday was looking unlikely.
On the heels of Tuesday's blowout session for Wall Street, the streaming-video maker delivered boffo results. But investors must now cool their heels until next week to hear from Amazon (AMZN) and Microsoft (MSFT), with (FB) Apple (AAPL) due the week after.
While plenty of blue chips will report between now and then, the cadre of techy names referred to as FAANGs, will draw special attention from investors, as they have been the group--by dint of their market value and investor lust for growth--that has sustained the current bull-market rally, even if 2018 is looking decidedly more volatile.
Outside of Tuesday's burst higher, the broader downturn in equity markets, and FAANG names specifically, has created a degree of uneasiness within the FAANG stalwarts.
Thus far investors have been of two camps: The FOMO, or fear of missing out, set, who have helped to drive stocks higher, with those market participants piling on to companies that have been enjoying better-than-average share-price gains. And those on the FOIAE, or fear of it all ending, side. That is those who fret that each political conflagration or pricey sector could be the final undoing of a decadelong bull market.
Only time will tell who is right.
That leads us to our call of the day, from Kevin Muir of the Macro Tourist blog (http://www.themacrotourist.com/posts/2018/10/16/factors/), who raises questions over an investment strategy that has been red-hot over the past year, but which may be showing signs of decline. Take a look at his chart, which shows the biggest factors that have been driving U.S. stock performance over the past year:
Take note of the factor which has crested to the top, and by a pretty big margin: three-month target-price changes. "This means that mindlessly following analyst 3-month target price changes was the smartest strategy over the past year from this list," wrote Muir.
The next biggest factor is U.S. Momentum, which Muir is a strategy by which investors buy the biggest risers over the last 12 months and selling their losers. "What about stuff like Price/Earnings or Price/Book ratios? Where are those fundamental factors? Surely, just chasing the hot stock can't be a portfolio strategy," he argues, but yeah that is what's been working for investors. Buying momentum stocks.
At the bottom of that above chart is one definitely not-hot strategy--value, which has gotten no breaks this year, Muir notes.
Over the past two-years that momentum strategy looks like a clear winner, but he's more interested in this chart that shows what's been going on over the last 12 months.
In short, momentum has been relinquishing ground or at least losing, well, momentum.
"'Momentum' is no longer being rewarded quite as heavily, and in fact, during the latest equity market sell off, the stocks that had performed the best over the past year led the move to the downside," said Muir. End of that trend friend? We shall see.
The market
Dow , S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures are struggling. That's after Wednesday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stocks-poised-to-rise-after-mondays-tech-driven-selloff-2018-10-16) marked the best day for the Dow and Nasdaq since late March and S&P 500 also bounded higher.
Gold and oil are down, but the dollar is up, largely against the pound on a big day for Brexit talks and after U.K. inflation data.
Check out the Market Snapshot column (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stocks-poised-to-rise-after-mondays-tech-driven-selloff-2018-10-16) for the latest action.
Europe is trading flat, while Asia saw lots of gains (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-jump-following-wall-streets-big-gains-2018-10-16), with the Nikkei jumping 1.2%.
The chart
Our chart of the day comes from Standard Chartered (h/t Holger Zschaepitz from Die Welt). It isn't an easy one on the stomach as it predicts a gut-wrenching 20% drop for the S&P 500 toward the end of this year and early into next year, as central-bank balance sheets start to shrivel up and that easy-money spigot really gets turned off.
(https://twitter.com/Schuldensuehner/status/1052469136809439232)
Here's that chart again in case the tweet isn't clear enough:
The buzz
Netflix (NFLX) shares are rocketing higher after blowing out Wall Street forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/netflix-earnings-send-stock-surging-suggest-huge-decline-was-an-aberration-2018-10-16) on better-than-expected earnings and subscriber numbers, with plans to add nearly 10 million more streaming video enthusiasts in the fourth quarter. It announced plans to ditch free trials (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/netflix-is-ditching-freeloaders-from-subscriber-forecasts-after-volatile-stock-moves-2018-10-16) in 2019, which could mean less volatile shares. However, KeyBanc analysts downgraded shares (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/netflix-downgraded-at-keybanc-due-to-pace-of-spend-and-length-of-time-for-a-return-2018-10-17), citing cash burn and the time it will take to see a return. That fan base, though...
(https://twitter.com/StephenKing/status/1052375524192980993)
IBM (IBM) is down after a revenue miss (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ibm-stock-falls-after-revenue-misses-street-view-2018-10-16), while United Continental Holdings (UAL)(UAL)is up on its results (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/united-stock-up-4-after-earnings-2018-10-16). Abbott Laboratories (ABT) is on the earnings docket this morning, with Alcoa (AH.TH) coming after the bell.
New and gruesome details have emerged (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/grisly-new-details-emerge-in-saudi-journalists-disappearance-2018-10-16) over the suspected death of journalist Jamal Khashoggi, who disappeared after entering Saudi Arabia's Istanbul consulate two weeks ago. Trump criticized world-wide condemnation (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-compares-condemnation-of-saudis-over-missing-journalist-to-kavanaugh-hearing-2018-10-16) of the Saudis over the incident in an interview with the Associated Press Tuesday, compared it with Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh's confirmation hearing.
It is "moment of truth" day for U.K. Prime Minister Theresa May who will address EU leaders in Brussels Wednesday and try to win them over with a Brexit deal. But a no-deal scenario (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/with-no-deal-brexit-risk-on-the-rise-analysts-see-uncertain-path-for-pound-2018-10-16) and markets upheaval are what some are bracing for.
MarketWatch exclusive: The dying days of Theranos (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-last-days-of-theranos-the-financials-were-as-overhyped-as-the-blood-tests-2018-10-16) and how its young CEO touted financial projections that never materialized based on technology that she never delivered.
The economy
Housing starts and building permits are on the way this morning, followed by Fed minutes for the latest meeting.
